faqs.a: The nth root of x is the number which, multiplied by itself n times, gives x. So the cube root of 27 is 3 because 3 × 3 × 3 = 27.
Yes — odd roots of negatives are real. The cube root of -27 is -3. Even roots of negatives are not real numbers, so the calculator shows a note.

root-calculator.formula:
nth root of x = x^(1/n)
x ≥ 0: always defined
x < 0 and n odd: -((-x)^(1/n))
x < 0 and n even: not a real number
howTo: Enter the root degree n (2 to 100), or tap a preset.

keyFacts: The nth root undoes raising to the nth power.

root-calculator.quickAnswer: The nth root of x is the number that gives x when multiplied by itself n times: x^(1/n). The square root of 16 is 4, and the cube root of 27 is 3. Negative numbers have real odd roots — the cube root of -27 is -3 — but no real even roots.

root-calculator.workedExample:
Find the cube root of 27.

n = 3, x = 27.
∛27 = 27^(1/3) = 3.

Verification: 3³ = 27. Correct.

Now try x = -27 with n = 3:
∛(-27) = -3, because (-3)³ = -27. The calculator handles the sign correctly.
